title: Meet EchoBird
summary: Understand apps, accounts, models, and routing groups, then choose the right starting point.
body:
EchoBird brings AI tools, accounts, and models together on one desktop. Keep using the clients you know, prepare and manage your setup here, and return your attention to what you want to create.

Start with these four concepts

ConceptThink of it asWhere to manage it
App / AgentThe tool that carries out tasks or chats with you, such as a coding client or desktop assistantApp Desktop
AccountYour identity with a provider, together with its plan, authorization, and quotaAccounts
ModelA callable API configuration: endpoint, credentials, and model IDModels
Routing groupAn arrangement of available sources that gives your tools one local endpointSmart Routes

Choose a starting point

  • Already have an official account? Detect or install the app, add your account, then select and apply it in App Desktop. This suits users who want to keep using an existing subscription.
  • Already have an API key? Save the configuration and test its connection speed in Models, then verify actual replies in a supported tool. This suits users who want to reuse an API service.
  • Have several model sources? Arrange primary and fallback sources in Smart Routes so your tools can use one endpoint.
  • Want to use your own hardware? Start a service in Local LLM, then let other supported features use it.

Managing, selecting, and applying are separate steps

Saving an account or model tells EchoBird to remember it. Selecting an entry indicates what you intend to use. Applying the configuration makes that choice take effect in the corresponding tool. Keeping these steps separate lets you maintain multiple configurations centrally without changing a working client just by browsing a page.

Get one tool working first

For your first setup, choose one tool you already know. Complete the full sequence—save a source, select the tool, apply the configuration, and make a real request—before adding more accounts, fallback models, or desktop features.

How the features fit together

App Desktop is your starting point. Accounts and Models provide available sources, Smart Routes organizes them, and AI Assistant carries out the tasks you describe. Voice Input reduces typing, Usage Island keeps status on your desktop, and TokenPet adds companionship to your work. News, My AI Career, and Local LLM can be enabled as needed.

Read Quick Start first. If your sources are already configured, go straight to Workflow Guides.

title: Quick Start
summary: Go from installing EchoBird to making your first tool work.
body:
Install and open EchoBird

  1. Choose an installer from the official download area that matches your operating system and processor. Windows, macOS, and Linux packages are not interchangeable.
  2. Complete the system installation process and open EchoBird. On your first launch, check App Desktop to see which tools have been detected.
  3. If an installed tool is missing, click Refresh, then use the tool-path settings to check the executable location.

Prepare one working source

Choose either of the following routes. You do not need to configure both an account and an API to get started.

What you haveNext stepWhere to go afterward
An official account with a supported serviceOpen Accounts, add the account, and complete the service's authorization processSelect the corresponding tool and account in App Desktop
An API key from a providerOpen Models, enter the real endpoint and model ID, save, and click Test LatencySelect a tool in App Desktop that supports this model configuration

A web chat account password is not an API key. Domestic, international, subscription, and other service endpoints from the same provider may also require different credentials.

Apply your first configuration and launch

  1. Select an installed tool in App Desktop. The right panel shows the account or model options supported by that tool.
  2. Select the source you just saved. Official accounts and API models are mutually exclusive: selecting one clears the other selection.
  3. Read the current main action at the bottom and the launch/configuration-write options, then apply or launch as appropriate. The actual client's buttons change with the situation.
  4. In the opened tool, check the active identity or model and send a simple request, such as “Briefly introduce what you can do.”

How to confirm the setup works

  • The tool opens normally and a real request receives a normal reply.
  • When using an official account, the identity shown in the tool is the account you intended.
  • When using an API, the endpoint, model ID, and credentials match. If routing is involved, the local routing endpoint is available.
  • Keep the exact error if something fails. Authorization, model IDs, protocols, networking, and installation paths are different issues and should be checked separately.

What to try next

To reuse configurations across tools, read Models. For fallback sources, read Smart Routes. To reduce manual installation work, read AI Assistant. If your tool already works, keep that successful configuration and add features gradually.

title: Interface and Navigation
summary: Understand the left sidebar, the entries at the top of App Desktop, and each page’s main workspace.
body:
Use the left sidebar to switch workspaces

PageThe question it helps answer
App DesktopWhich tool should I open, and which source should it use?
ModelsWhich reusable API services and model configurations do I have?
AccountsWhat is the status of my accounts, plans, and quotas?
Smart RoutesHow should I organize model sources and fallback priorities for my tools?
Voice InputHow do I configure recording, recognition, and text processing?
AI AssistantCan I describe a goal and let the assistant carry it out?
News / My AI Career / Local LLMAdditional workspaces you can enable as needed

Other entries at the top of App Desktop

My shows your app entries, while Store lets you browse tools that are not installed. Pets, Plugins, and Usage Island at the top manage TokenPet, extensions, and desktop usage displays respectively. You do not need to find an app icon with the same name first.

Smart Routes's Configuration and Statistics views also have separate roles: one organizes sources, while the other shows request outcomes and trends.

Understanding the main area, right panel, and bottom action

  • Main area: Shows the current page's apps, models, accounts, conversations, or settings.
  • Right panel: Provides configuration, sources, targets, or details for the current selection. Its controls may change when you select another tool.
  • Main action at the bottom: Applies the current selection as a configuration, launch, or installation request. Read the button and options before proceeding.
  • Back and Forward: Return to previously visited locations. They do not undo configurations, commands, or installations that have already run.

If you cannot find a page

Open Settings at the lower left and check whether the optional page is enabled. Local LLM also depends on the capabilities included in your edition. If a tool has no account section, Image button, or 1M button, it generally does not expose that capability; it does not mean the feature is missing everywhere.

Pages and buttons may differ from the interactive demo on the website homepage. The demo uses sample data and simplified flows; follow the current client interface for real operations.

title: Settings and Personalization
summary: Adjust the interface, language, optional pages, and everyday app behavior.
body:
Where to open Settings

Use Settings at the bottom of the sidebar. Settings are organized into General, Appearance, and Language. Before changing anything, distinguish app-wide settings from the settings for an individual feature.

General settings

SettingPurpose
UI scaleAdjust interface size for your screen and reading preferences; try automatic scaling first
When closing the windowChoose to exit, minimize to the system tray, or ask each time
Launch at startupControl whether EchoBird opens when you sign in to your system
Auto-claim rewardsManage supported automatic claiming; not every service offers rewards
Sensitive information protectionIdentify and strengthen protection for keys, tokens, passwords, and similar information when using Smart Routes; related mappings are saved locally
Record statisticsControl statistics recording; this does not stop a running model service
Optional pagesShow AI Latest News, My AI Career, and Local LLM as needed

Appearance and backgrounds

Choose a color palette and Light, Dark, or Follow System mode. Background options include None, Character Flow, Carbon Fiber, and Basalt, so you can match your desktop and reading preferences. If text is too small, adjust UI scale before changing your screen resolution.

Usage Island and Voice Island also have their own theme and size settings. Changing the main window's appearance does not automatically set every parameter in those features to the same value.

Language

The current choices are English, Simplified Chinese, Traditional Chinese, and Japanese. Check the interface after selecting a language. Model IDs, errors returned by providers, and third-party content may remain in their original language; do not alter a model ID merely to translate it.

Check here when an entry is missing

If you do not need news or activity history, disable the corresponding page; you can enable it again later. Local LLM also depends on whether your installed edition includes that capability.

Desktop activation and sources for Usage Island are managed on the Usage Island page. Voice Input needs a working channel first. Page visibility, feature activation, and service running status are separate controls.

title: Workflow Guides
summary: Connect individual pages into useful workflows and understand what each step achieves.
body:
Route 1: Keep using your subscription

  1. App Desktop: Detect or install the client you normally use.
  2. Accounts: Add your official account and check its identity and authorization.
  3. App Desktop: Select the client and account, then apply the configuration and launch.
  4. The actual client: Check the identity and make a request. Return to Accounts to refresh quota when needed.

Result: Manage account status centrally while using familiar tools. Adding an account and switching a client remain clearly separate steps.

Route 2: Reuse a model across tools

  1. Models: Save the endpoint, key, and model ID, then click Test Latency to check connectivity and latency.
  2. App Desktop: Select this model for a supported tool and apply its configuration.
  3. A second tool: Reuse the same model entry, applying it with a protocol that tool supports.
  4. Verify: Make a request in each tool to confirm the configuration has taken effect beyond simply being saved in EchoBird.

Result: Less repeated data entry and a clear record of your model sources. Protocol and feature support still depend on each tool and model.

Route 3: Primary models and fallback sources

  1. Verify your primary and fallback APIs in Models. You can also prepare supported account sources.
  2. Create a group in Smart Routes, configure the actual endpoint and key, and arrange sources by priority.
  3. Connect your coding client to that group and make a real request.
  4. Review completion and failover results in Statistics, and add your usual usage sources to Usage Island.

Result: Keep the client's connection relatively stable while adjusting sources centrally. When quotas or failures change, status information helps you decide what to do next instead of blindly repeating requests.

Route 4: From an error back to work

  1. Check installation status in App Desktop and keep the exact error if a tool cannot launch.
  2. Open AI Assistant and describe the tool, operating system, error, and desired result.
  3. Watch the environment checks and tool output, handling permissions through system prompts when needed.
  4. Return to App Desktop, refresh detection, and launch the tool to confirm the issue is resolved.

Result: Connect installation troubleshooting with a real acceptance check. The assistant's summary explains the process; a successful launch confirms the outcome.

Route 5: Speak your request and stay focused

Configure a channel in Voice Input and test the microphone, then place the cursor in AI Assistant or your usual tool. Dictate the task, check the recognized text, and send it. Monitor status with Usage Island as you work. Tokens recorded through Smart Routes can also contribute to pet growth on the Pets page.

Route 6: Your hardware, your model service

Prepare model files and an engine in Local LLM, start the service, and then let supported model entries and AI Assistant use it. If something fails, distinguish a service that has not started, an unavailable model, and a failed task. This lets you verify “running the model” separately from “having the model do something.”

title: Feedback and Release Notes
summary: Gather useful details, choose a feedback channel, and learn what changed in each release.
body:
Open Feedback

Click Feedback in the client's title bar or open the corresponding page from the system menu. This page helps you prepare information and choose an external submission channel; it is not a ticket form that automatically uploads everything.

Report a problem

  1. Record your operating system and architecture, EchoBird version, page and tool names, and the steps that trigger the problem.
  2. When troubleshooting an error, click the button to copy the latest 30 log entries. Copying does not send them; you still need to paste the logs into your report.
  3. Use the GitHub entry on the page to create an issue. The Simplified Chinese interface also provides a Gitcode feedback entry.
  4. Describe the expected and actual results, attach relevant screenshots or logs, and check for accounts, keys, or other sensitive information before submitting.

Other interface languages also provide an email button that copies hi@echobird.ai. It does not send a message automatically. Continue in your own email app to contact us.

Suggest an app or improvement

You can use the same external feedback entries to describe a tool you would like supported or a workflow you want improved. Include the tool's name, official website, use case, and the steps you currently perform manually. This is more useful than simply asking for support. You do not need to copy error logs before submitting a feature suggestion.

Release notes and installing updates are different

Release Notes in the title bar opens a dialog with the version, release date, and changes in the corresponding language. The dialog may also open once after a first installation or an upgrade to a version whose notes you have not read.

Opening release notes does not immediately install an update. To update the software, continue through the client's download or installation entry. If the notes fail to load, try again later; already loaded content is retained where possible.

title: Troubleshooting
summary: Identify the layer where a problem occurs, then check the relevant settings.
body:
The account was added, but the client did not switch

Adding an account only saves it. Return to App Desktop, select the corresponding client and account, run the current main action, and check whether the running client needs further attention. A highlighted selection alone does not mean every open window has switched.

The model was saved, but the tool still uses the old model

Check whether you applied the model in App Desktop, whether the tool supports its protocol, and whether configuration-write options allow the change. First click Test Latency in Models to check connectivity, then send a request in the actual tool or AI Assistant to verify the reply and active configuration. This is more useful than repeatedly saving the same entry.

The model cannot connect or a routed request fails

  1. Direct model: check the endpoint, key, model ID, and the service's regional or plan-specific entry.
  2. Smart Routes: confirm EchoBird is still running and the tool uses the endpoint and key shown by the current group.
  3. Check source authorization, enabled status, and the model catalog. Distinguish a single upstream failure from failure of the overall request.
  4. Explicitly test or refresh on the relevant page, then make another real request. Keep the original error message.

Why is the balance or quota blank?

A service may answer requests without providing a usage-query API. Some sources need additional usage configuration, and some expose only certain metrics. Refresh explicitly and check authorization and service documentation. An unknown value does not mean zero. Different periods and units also cannot simply be added together.

Installation failed or a tool was not detected

First confirm the vendor supports your operating system and architecture, then check the network, permissions, dependencies, and installation output. After installation, return to App Desktop and refresh. If the tool is still missing, check its executable path. Even if AI Assistant reports completion, launch the tool to verify it.

Speech was recognized, but the text was not inserted

Copy the retained recognition result first so you do not have to repeat yourself. Then check input focus, system permissions, and shortcut conflicts. On macOS, check Accessibility permissions. On Linux/Wayland, follow the bridging capabilities actually supported by your desktop.

I used many tokens, but TokenPet did not change

Pet credit comes from new records in the Smart Routes ledger, not all consumption in websites or third-party clients. Confirm Record Statistics is enabled, requests pass through Smart Routes, and upstream responses contain recognizable usage data. TokenPet is not an API balance.

How to send a useful report

Include your operating system and architecture, EchoBird version, page and tool names, the steps you performed, the original error, and your expected result. Hide accounts and keys before sharing screenshots. Contact us through GitHub Issues or hi@echobird.ai.
